incidents.vector: An attacker used a LiteLLM master key exposed in a May leak to gain GitHub access and publish a malicious PyPI package (v1.107.0) containing credential-harvesting malware.
incidents.impact: The malicious package was downloaded roughly 49,000 times; stolen AWS cloud credentials were tested within hours in a scheme known as 'LLMjacking' to run AI services at victims' expense.

incidents.vector: Threat actors compromised customer accounts as part of a broader, industry-wide campaign against AI infrastructure providers.
incidents.impact: Customer credentials and AI API keys were stolen; access to the compromised AI infrastructure was reportedly resold on underground forums.

incidents.victim: Dahua surveillance camera operators in Ukraine, including government and military users
incidents.vector: Exploitation of Dahua's Easy4IP cloud remote-access feature via guessable device serial numbers, weak or default passwords, and outdated firmware (CVE-2021-33044, CVE-2021-33045).
incidents.impact: Hackers gained unauthorized access to internet-connected cameras and video recorders, changed device settings and created unauthorized user accounts; the scale of compromise in Ukraine has not been disclosed.

incidents.vector: Intruders gained access to internal business systems via a learning management system and a customer relationship management platform.
incidents.impact: Internal business systems were compromised; the company found no evidence attackers pivoted to its public customer clouds.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached an internal platform via an unnamed CRM tool used by business partners to sell energy contracts.
incidents.impact: ENGIE is notifying customers of its French gas supply business of a security breach involving an internal platform.

incidents.vector: An 'infinite mint' smart-contract exploit allowed attackers to create unauthorized tokens.
incidents.impact: Attackers created and stole $2.7 million worth of tokens.

incidents.vector: Social engineering via social media, phone calls, texts and dating sites lured victims into fake cryptocurrency investment platforms.
incidents.impact: At least 174 U.S. residents were defrauded of nearly $37 million; proceeds were laundered through a Bahamas bank, converted to Tether, and distributed to Cambodia-based scam networks. A suspect was extradited from the Netherlands and arraigned; eight co-conspirators have already pleaded guilty.

incidents.victim: Enterprise GitHub users (dozens of organizations, including private repositories)
incidents.vector: Attackers use GitHub tokens stolen via infostealer malware and prior supply-chain leaks to plant a disguised 'sync-check' GitHub Actions workflow that prints repository secrets to a workflow log, then exfiltrates and deletes the log via the GitHub API.
incidents.impact: More than 13,500 malicious branches were created across over 850 compromised GitHub accounts; cloud credentials from affected organizations were used to enumerate AWS Secrets Manager at roughly a dozen companies.

incidents.vector: A flaw in eMudhra's April 2025 key-generation ceremony produced critically weak private keys (as little as 3-8 bits of entropy instead of 384) for eight intermediate certificate authority certificates, making the keys trivially recoverable.
incidents.impact: Six compromised TLS and two code-signing intermediate certificates could have been used to impersonate websites or forge signed code; Chrome, Mozilla, Apple and Microsoft revoked or blocked the affected certificates. No malicious exploitation has been observed yet.

incidents.victim: Government and commercial websites running PHP (global, including European government sites)
incidents.vector: Two unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaws in PHP core (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619, dubbed 'PHP2Shell') affect every PHP build since version 5.4 and are exploitable via a plain HTTP request before any application code runs.
incidents.impact: Roughly 22.6 million internet-facing PHP instances were exposed; several European government websites went offline; scanning and targeted exploitation attempts began within hours of disclosure, though confirmed large-scale compromise has not been established.

incidents.victim: Organizations across education, financial services, healthcare, government and other sectors (global)
incidents.vector: Ransomware operators (including groups tracked as Qilin, Inc, and others using Settra ransomware) exploit the PAN-OS GlobalProtect authentication-bypass flaw CVE-2026-0257 for initial VPN access, then move laterally via RDP and SMB and pivot into vCenter/ESXi infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Multiple organizations have been breached since June 2026; attackers disabled hypervisor security controls, performed offline domain-credential theft from virtual disks, and deployed ransomware.

incidents.vector: A suspected Chinese-speaking actor (tracked as TAG-217) used the AI-assisted penetration-testing framework ARTEX to opportunistically test for and exploit weaknesses across multiple institutions.
incidents.impact: Personal data belonging to at least 68,000 people was exposed across seven financial institutions; one breach exposed an outsourced developer's data, while another resulted in theft of customer data.

incidents.vector: State-directed North Korean IT workers use stolen identities, paid facilitators and 'laptop farms' to obtain remote technology jobs at U.S. companies while concealing their location and nationality.
incidents.impact: Revenue funds North Korea's weapons programs; the scheme poses an insider-threat and intellectual-property-theft risk to employers, and facilitators have been threatened and extorted.
